chunks: Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Abu Yazid Muhammad b. Yahya b. Khalid b. Yazid al-Maruzi narrated to us in Ray in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal in the year 302 AH. He said: Ishaq b. Ibrahim al-Hanthali narrated to us in the year 238 AH -- and he is known as Ishaq b. Rahuwayh. He said: Yahya b. Yahya narrated to us. He said: Hisham narrated to us from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq who said:
While we were with Abdullah b. Mas'ud showing our codices to him, a young man said to him: Did your Prophet tell you how many caliphs there would be after him?

He said: You are young in age, and indeed no one before you has asked me about this. Yes, our Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) told us that there would be twelve caliphs after him, like the number of chiefs of the Children of Israel.

key_terms.بني إسرائيل: Children of Israel -- the Israelites, descendants of Prophet Jacob
key_terms.خليفة: Caliph/successor -- one who succeeds the Prophet in leadership of the Muslim community
key_terms.عهد: Told/covenanted/charged -- a prophetic instruction or testament
key_terms.نقباء: Chiefs/leaders (naqib) -- appointed representatives, here referring to the twelve chiefs God appointed over the Israelites (Quran 5:12)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about twelve caliphs after him?
ai.summary: Abdullah b. Mas'ud, a senior companion of the Prophet, was asked by a young man about the number of successors after the Prophet. Ibn Mas'ud expressed surprise at the question, noting that no one had asked him this before. He then confirmed that the Prophet (SAWW) had told them there would be twelve caliphs after him, equal to the number of chiefs (naqib) of the Children of Israel -- a reference to Quran 5:12. This hadith is one of the most widely transmitted traditions on the concept of the Twelve Successors, narrated in both Sunni and Shia sources.
